headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from Opik’s broad egress feeding Rasa’s multi-channel customer-support surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Opik can ingest and emit evaluation content over a REST API, while Rasa consumes user-facing text/voice across chat channels. A shared handoff path is plausible if Opik outputs are copied into Rasa prompts or training data, so injected instructions could cross the boundary. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are pasted into Rasa training examples or dialogue prompts, injection can propagate.
IF Rasa treats imported text as authoritative instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any Opik output is imported into Rasa.
Prefix imported content as untrusted and strip instruction-like markup.
Use a separate staging workspace for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Opik through Rasa ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Opik has broad network egress and Rasa handles text and voice through external messaging APIs. If either side shares transcripts, prompts, or evaluation artifacts, sensitive conversation data can leave the workspace. The profiles do not show shared isolation or explicit retention controls, so the leakage pathway exists in default integrations rather than only unusual setups.
conditions: IF transcripts or evaluation logs are forwarded from Opik into Rasa channels, data can leak to external services.
IF either integration stores customer text in shared logs, both systems may expose the same data class.
mitigations: Disable sharing of raw transcripts between systems.
Review and redact logs before export.
Use separate credentials and workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: configure field-level redaction on all message payloads.
requires-engineering: add retention limits and deletion workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Opik exposes REST API egress, and Rasa supports multiple external messaging APIs, but neither profile shows unrestricted shared filesystem or overlapping write scopes. Rasa also reports no multiple-instance support, which reduces concurrency conflict rather than increasing it. The main overlap is integration-level, so the conflict risk is limited and not clearly dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable external resource, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator routes both agents into one shared queue without locking, writes may race.
mitigations: Assign separate queues or topics per agent.
Avoid shared mutable files or databases.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Opik is an evaluation/observability system and Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue. If Opik-generated judgments or summaries are fed into Rasa without verification, Rasa may treat them as authoritative and propagate errors to users. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Opik summaries are used as ground truth for Rasa responses, errors can cascade.
IF Rasa auto-replies from imported evaluation artifacts, incorrect facts may be surfaced to customers.
mitigations: Require human review before Rasa uses Opik outputs.
Mark Opik outputs as advisory only.
Compare outputs against source records before sending replies.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and fallback handling.
requires-engineering: separate evaluation data from customer-facing dialogue state.

E_compliance.rationale: Opik is an observability/evaluation tool with broad egress, while Rasa processes text and voice in customer-support channels. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if customer conversations are exported from one system into the other. No certifications or residency guarantees are documented, so the safest reading is a moderate compliance gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts are copied into Opik logs, retention policy mismatches can arise.
IF either deployment stores EU or regulated data in a different region than the other, residency issues can occur.
mitigations: Inventory which data classes flow between systems.
Set matching retention periods for shared artifacts.
Restrict exports of regulated transcripts.
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows across both systems.
